headline: High-risk default interaction: agentic-flow can modify local state and use MCP, while firecrawl has broad network egress and API access, creating leakage and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agentic-flow can use MCP and stdin/stdout, so if firecrawl outputs scraped web content into a shared MCP or file bridge, prompt injection is plausible. firecrawl is a crawler/scraper that handles raw web content, which is the classic attacker-controlled input. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF firecrawl-sourced content is passed into agentic-flow prompts or MCP messages without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF the two agents share a clipboard, file, or MCP channel, attacker-controlled web text can reach agentic-flow instructions.
mitigations: Disable direct prompt ingestion of scraped text.
Add a fixed allowlist of fields extracted from firecrawl output.
Insert a human review step before agentic-flow executes instructions from firecrawl.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all firecrawl outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agentic-flow touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures, while firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, and API keys. If they share a workspace or MCP bridge, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other and then out through firecrawl's broad network egress. No isolation is documented, so the shared-data pathway is credible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or files, sensitive prompts or keys can be exposed.
IF firecrawl is given agentic-flow artifacts to scrape or transmit, those artifacts may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep separate directories and credentials for each agent.
Do not pass secrets or signatures into firecrawl.
Restrict firecrawl to non-sensitive URLs only.
Review outbound requests from firecrawl before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agentic-flow can execute shell commands, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; firecrawl exposes API/CLI and supports MCP-compatible client use. If both are pointed at the same repo or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git-state races are plausible. The profiles do not show locking, so the conflict pathway exists in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator runs multiple instances concurrently without locks, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize git writes with a lock.
Avoid concurrent package installs in the same environment.
Use read-only mounts for firecrawl when possible.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agentic-flow can generate outputs from prompts and background tasks, and firecrawl can scrape or act through API endpoints. If firecrawl consumes agentic-flow output as authoritative instructions or facts, errors can cascade into external actions or bad crawls. Because no verification layer is documented, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF firecrawl uses agentic-flow output as instructions without verification, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF agentic-flow routes scraped results into downstream tasks automatically, one bad output can fan out across work products.
mitigations: Require schema validation on all agentic-flow outputs before firecrawl uses them.
Add a human approval step for any external action.
Log and diff firecrawl inputs against expected templates.
Limit firecrawl to read-only scraping modes.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: agentic-flow touches repository metadata, task prompts, and performance metrics, while firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, and API keys. If regulated or personal data is scraped into firecrawl and then stored or processed by agentic-flow, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No compliance controls are documented for either agent, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is scraped by firecrawl and then retained in agentic-flow artifacts, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF either agent logs screenshots or prompts containing personal data, retention policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through either agent.
Set short log-retention windows for both tools.
Redact screenshots and prompts before storage.
Confirm data-processing terms for firecrawl before use.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
